newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian air traffic staff to strike on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian air traffic staff to strike on Wednesday.

text.p: Belgian air traffic controllers will stop work for half a day on Wednesday afternoon, joining a national demonstration planned by public sector workers' unions, officials said on Tuesday.

"Belgian air traffic management will go on strike because of the lack of consultation and information on new plans which effectively eliminate their jobs," the Federation of Transport Workers' Unions in the European Union (FST) said in a statement.
FST spokesman Giancarlo Crivellaro said the strike action, between 1200 and 1600 GMT, could cause delays at Brussels National Airport but was unlikely to hit other Belgian airports.
"The order (for action) has been given but it remains to be seen to what extent it will be followed," he told Reuters. Not all air traffic controllers were members of a union.
In the statement, the FST said Belgian air traffic controllers were worried that part of their work could be moved to a new air traffic control centre based in Maastricht, the Netherlands.
The FST said "secret negotiations" between five countries about such a centre were going on within Eurocontrol, the Europe-wide air traffic control organisation.
No one at Eurocontrol was immediately available to comment.
